broader_coverage.reasoning: The objective is not outside general S-shaped allocation theory: maximizing 1-q_p(x)q_p(B-x) is equivalent by the strictly monotone logarithm to maximizing g_p(x)+g_p(B-x), where g_p=-log q_p has one convex-to-concave inflection. A general theorem applying to all S-shaped utilities could therefore dominate a portion of the new claim. The inspected accessible statements and algorithms do not imply the exact all-budget root and sharp two-sided quantifiers; the missing historical bodies remain genuine coverage risks, not declared non-covering.

originality.rationale: The sharp uniform budget theorem and its two opposing real-quantifier clauses are not implied by an earlier fixed example with the exact same Poisson viability objective, nor by the inspected primary ecological-estimator or one-encounter expectation results. Generic sigmoid allocation papers give structural background, with a frank residual historical-priority risk where primary bodies were inaccessible. The result is not presented as discovering asymmetric Poisson allocation per se.
residual_risks: The optimization is exactly a sum of two identical convex-then-concave utilities after taking negative logs of the no-confirmation probabilities. The 1970 Vicentini generic class directly includes this setting; only its abstract was accessible, so broad historical coverage cannot be ruled out.
The 1970 Vicentini memoir and 1974 Ginsberg paper were only available through bibliographic description, not primary full text; a stronger general theorem could have covered this exact threshold.
Generic S-shaped allocation theory may contain an unindexed analytically equivalent result.
An earlier fixed Poisson-quorum example establishes asymmetry, not the present sharp universal onset; claims of novelty are explicitly restricted accordingly.

value.rationale: The universal dimensionless threshold is a natural sharp decision boundary: below 8.402... no occupancy probability justifies unequal positive allocation, while above it at least one does. It resolves the exact domain of validity of a common concentrated-or-even design heuristic, gives a reproducible robust rational counterexample, and proves eventual return to balance at fixed prevalence. A continuous all-budget structural result, not a thin parameter substitution or mere finite search.
